chunks: It is God who raised the skies without support, as you can see, then assumed His throne, and enthralled the sun and the moon (so that) each runs to a predetermined course. He disposes all affairs, distinctly explaining every sign that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God raising the heavens without visible pillars?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of *Tawhid* by emphasizing God's absolute sovereignty and the subjugation of celestial bodies to His will, serving as a sign for those who reflect. The mention of 'managing affairs' (*Yudabbiru al-amr*) is often linked to the role of the Imams as the practical executors of divine decree in the earthly realm. This assurance of certainty (*Tawqin*) regarding the Hereafter reinforces the Shia emphasis on *Ma'ad* (resurrection) as the ultimate purpose of creation.
